title: Great app! A few issues...
body:
I purchased a Samsung Galaxy Fit watch a year ago, and I immediately downloaded this app. For the most part it has worked excellently for me, and I had no problems whatsoever. But I did have some problems, some of which defied the purpose of the app:

-There was a two-month period where the app didn’t track my heart rate at all. I have a huge gap in my tracking, and since this is the only way to keep my heart rate readings without writing them down, I found this especially annoying. It works now, but every now and again I will have a gap of a few days in my graph.

-You need a SIM Card to use the app. For a while my phone didn’t have a SIM Card, so I had to use the app on a device that wasn’t mine.

-I’m slightly confused about a certain feature. Stress tracking is something that is shown on the website for my watch, and in pictures of Samsung Health, but I don’t seem to have it. Is this because I am an IOS user?

-How come you can’t be below the age of thirteen to use this app? I noticed this a while back and it seems strange to me. There are kids who have Samsung products and who would happily use this app if they could put In their proper age.

All in all, great app. I would suggest it for anyone who wants to use it. Just a few problems. Thank you!

title: Disappointed in the accuracy
body:
I’d like to be able to record portions that I eat, but the app doesn’t give me the choice- it’s either one portion or 1/2 a portion, and often the portion size is not defined. 
Also, the sleep recording is poor. If you sleep for a little bit, wake up, and then go back to sleep again after an hour or so, usually that is either not recorded or shown as one long sleep. And if you are recording manually, you’re not given any opportunity to record more than one “session” per calendar date. 
I’m finding that much of what is supposed to be automatically recorded is highly inaccurate, and there does not seem to be a way to correct it manually. So the summary reports are next to useless and don’t reflect what actually happened. 
Need options for far more details and choices!!!!

I have been wearing an Apple Watch, a Fitbit Charge 2, and my new Galaxy Watch together for several days. The Fitbit and Apple Watch report very similar steps, stairs, active minutes, sleep times, etc. The Galaxy Watch stats are always much lower (fewer steps, stairs, etc). I have tried wearing it tight, loose, in different places on my wrist — no difference. When I check on forums, this seems to be a VERY common problem. Samsung needs to get their act together. Why would you release an app without checking if it matches the stats being reported by competitors?? It is baffling.

If this is a software problem, get it fixed!
